producer_report.summary:
The verifier stage grew because the verifier's cargo commands started on an empty build directory. The cause is read from the code, not timed per command. When build slots took over the checks' target directories, the link to the slot was dropped after every check command. Nothing linked the verifier's `target/verify` again, so each `cargo test` or `clippy` it ran for a behavior criterion compiled every third-party crate from scratch.

The fix is two new methods, `link_verifier_build` and `release_verifier_build`, in `run/checks.rs`, called around the verifier invocation in `verification_stage`. They take a build slot and link the verifier's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to the slot's warm directory. After the verifier ends and its snapshot is unlocked, the link is removed, workspace output is cleaned and the slot is freed, as after a check. If no slot is available, the verifier builds cold and a warning is printed; the job is not held.

The new test `the_verifier_builds_in_the_slots_warm_target_directory` checks that the verifier's build path is a link to a slot directory that already holds the check's third-party output, and that the link and slot are gone afterwards. It would fail without the fix. The existing `slot_max_gb` test is updated because the verifier is now the next use of the slot and deletes an over-limit directory.

The note `docs/design/verifier-stage-slowdown.md` and a CHANGELOG entry state the cause. They say the verifier median should fall below 3.5 over at least 20 landed jobs after the change.

I ran the targeted tests (70 in `produce_and_verify_order_tests`), clippy on `athena-core` and the policy scan. I did not run the full workspace `cargo test`.

checks_run.note: 70 tests including the new verifier test and the updated slot_max_gb test
run after moving the release to after unlock; the over-limit test was then updated and passed in the larger run
printed verifier 3.4 over the last 20 measured landed jobs

criteria_check.criterion: A note under docs/design/ (or the commit message) states the cause of the longer verifier stage and cites the code path or measurement that shows it, and the verifier can read it in the diff.
criteria_check.evidence: docs/design/verifier-stage-slowdown.md names the cause (the checks' slot link is dropped after each command, so the verifier's cargo commands start on an empty target/verify) and cites SnapExec::exec in run/checks.rs and verification_stage in run/verification.rs. It labels the cause as read from code, not timed per command, and cites the measured status output (verifier 3.4).

criteria_check.criterion: The diff removes the stated cause in crates/ code in the verifier path, for example by removing redundant work, and does not only change how the median is reported.
criteria_check.evidence: verification_stage now calls link_verifier_build before and release_verifier_build after the verifier invocation (run/verification.rs, run/checks.rs). status.rs is unchanged.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test` from the repository root: it passes, including a new or updated test that exercises the changed verifier behavior, and it fails if the cause is reintroduced.
criteria_check.evidence: New test the_verifier_builds_in_the_slots_warm_target_directory asserts the verifier's CARGO_TARGET_DIR is a link to the slot directory holding the check's third-party file. Without the link it is no link and an empty directory, so it fails. It passes, as does the updated slot_max_gb test and all 70 tests in produce_and_verify_order_tests. I did not run the full workspace suite.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran cargo clippy -p athena-core --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings (clean) and cargo fmt --all.

criteria_check.criterion: The change is a single focused fix with no unrelated edits, and the note says how the next throughput review should show verifier minutes per landed job falling below 3.5.
criteria_check.evidence: Edits are the one fix, its test, the note and a CHANGELOG entry. The note's last section says the verifier column should fall below 3.5 and move toward 3.1 over at least 20 landed jobs after the change, and what to do if it does not.

open_issues: The cause comes from reading the code and from the date of the slot change, not from per-command timings; the records hold only the verifier's wall time. The note says so and says what the next review should check.

The verifier now holds a build slot for its whole run. With max_check_slots = 1, another job's checks wait during it. If that costs throughput, raise max_check_slots or give the verifier its own slot class.
Demonstration runs (run/checks.rs) still build in the same target/verify path without a slot; I left them alone as out of focus.
I did not run the full workspace cargo test (9 to 11 minutes); Athena's checks will.
mistakes: My first version released the slot while the snapshot was still locked, so cargo clean failed and the slot was deleted. Two slot tests caught it; I moved the release after unlock.
I briefly left a dead block and a contradictory assertion in the edited slot_max_gb test, then removed both.
learnings: The status verifier column is only the verifier agent's invocation wall time (role_minutes over Role::Verifier). Checks, replay and demonstration runs are other stages.
SnapExec drops the slot link after every check command, so target/verify was empty for the verifier from the warm-target change on.
cargo clean fails inside a locked verifier snapshot, which refuses writes even to Cargo.lock. The slot release must run after vsnap.unlock().
Bash in this environment cannot pipe, so long test output cannot be trimmed.
desires: Per-command durations of the verifier's cargo commands in the invocation record, to confirm the cold-build cost directly.
A permitted way to read command output (tail, grep) in Bash; the test output was long.
